# DiskCleaner — Full Reference

> A macOS utility app that removes junk files, system logs, and clutter to free up disk space. Free trial includes 3 scans. $9.99 one-time purchase after — no subscription.

## Product

- Name: DiskCleaner
- Platform: macOS 13 Ventura through macOS 26 Tahoe
- Category: Utilities / Disk Cleaner / Mac Storage Optimizer

- Price: $9.99 one-time after trial (no subscription, covers up to 2 Macs, includes all future updates)

- Help: https://www.diskcleaner.pro/help

## What It Does

DiskCleaner scans junk on macOS and shows you every file before moving anything. Quick Scan covers seven categories; Deep Scan adds larger storage areas. All cleaned files go to macOS Trash — nothing is permanently deleted.

### Quick Scan — 7 categories

1. App Cache — cached data from installed applications
2. Browser Cache — supports 9 browsers: Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Opera, Arc, Vivaldi, Tor (all profiles)
3. Screenshots — old screenshots accumulated on your Desktop
4. Trash Contents — files already sitting in your Trash
5. System Logs — diagnostic logs and crash reports generated by macOS
6. Developer Data — Xcode derived data, iOS Simulators, CocoaPods, npm caches, build artifacts
7. App Leftovers — residual preference files and support data from uninstalled apps

### Deep Scan — additional locations

- Large Files — surfaces oversized files across the disk for review
- Downloads folder — forgotten installers, archives, and exported files
- iOS Backups — old device backups that can consume tens of gigabytes
- Mail Attachments — attachment caches from Mail, Outlook, Spark, and Canary
- External drive review — clutter visibility beyond the startup disk

## Special Modules

### App Uninstaller
Cleanly removes apps and all associated leftover files. Supports drag-and-drop from Finder or /Applications. Classifies leftover files by risk level (Safe, Caution, Review) before any removal. Shows every file for review with per-file checkboxes — same review model as cleanup scans.

### RAM Optimizer
Live memory telemetry dashboard. Displays Memory Pressure, Compressed Memory, Swap Used, and Page In/Out metrics in real time. One-tap safe memory optimization using the Apple-approved purge path. Shows the difference between what macOS reports as "used" vs what is actually freeable.

### Large Files Scanner
Surfaces oversized files across the entire disk. Displays file name, path, size, and last-accessed date. Per-file review before any action. Available in Deep Scan.

### Menu Bar App
Quick disk usage overview accessible from the Mac's menu bar at all times. Shows free space, triggers Quick Scan, and displays update badges without opening the main app.

## Safety Model

DiskCleaner never permanently deletes files. Every item moved goes to macOS Trash, where it can be reviewed and recovered. Users see a complete checklist of every file before anything is moved. Personal files, documents, photos, passwords, and iCloud data are never scanned or touched. Over 20 folder categories are explicitly protected.

## Risk Classification

Leftover files and cleanup candidates are classified into three categories:
- Safe — commonly safe to remove (e.g., cache, derived data, old logs)
- Caution — potentially useful files that the user should verify before removing
- Review — files that warrant manual review due to unusual location or size

## Permissions

DiskCleaner requests Full Disk Access and Home Folder access from macOS to enable comprehensive scanning. These permissions are optional — scans run at reduced scope without them. Finder Automation is used for Trash operations. No permission data is transmitted anywhere.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is DiskCleaner safe?
A: Yes. No file is ever permanently deleted. Everything goes to macOS Trash and is recoverable. You review every file before anything moves.

Q: Does DiskCleaner have a free trial?
A: Yes. DiskCleaner includes 3 free scans with no account required. After the trial, a one-time $9.99 purchase unlocks the app for up to 2 Macs including all future updates — no subscription.

Q: Does DiskCleaner collect my data or connect to the internet?
A: Never. It runs 100% locally. No network calls, no data collection, no account required. Your file names and disk contents never leave your machine.

Q: What macOS versions are supported?
A: macOS 13 Ventura through macOS 26 Tahoe. Universal Binary for Apple Silicon and Intel.

Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. $9.99 one-time purchase covers up to 2 Macs and includes all future updates — no subscription, no renewal, no upsells.

Q: How is it different from other Mac cleaners?
A: Most cleaners delete files silently. DiskCleaner shows you every single file first, with per-file checkboxes, and only moves files to Trash — never permanent deletion.

Q: What is the difference between Quick Scan and Deep Scan?
A: Quick Scan covers seven standard categories (App Cache, Browser Cache, Screenshots, Trash, System Logs, Developer Data, App Leftovers). Deep Scan adds larger storage areas including Downloads, iOS Backups, Large Files, Mail Attachments, and external drives.

Q: Does DiskCleaner require Full Disk Access?
A: Full Disk Access and Home Folder permissions are requested to enable comprehensive scanning. Scans work at reduced scope without them — DiskCleaner never demands access it doesn't have a specific use for.

Q: Does DiskCleaner clean Xcode derived data and iOS Simulators?
A: Yes. Developer Data is a dedicated Quick Scan category covering Xcode derived data, iOS Simulators (which alone can total 20–80 GB), CocoaPods caches, npm caches, and other build artifacts.

Q: Can I get a refund?
A: Yes. If purchased through the Mac App Store, Apple's standard 14-day refund policy applies. For direct purchases, contact customersupport@diskcleaner.pro.
